We've set up an eating place and we have a lot of vegetables and fruit waste. At the place we are we have a compost pile and after only two times we've figured out we have too much waste for the pile. If we will just trow stuff on it will be an overload pretty soon. My question is how can we compost a lot of vegetables and fruit. The place we can use is 1,5m by 4,5 meters. We were thinking to make This , but we need it to go fast. Please advice.
How to compost a lot of vegetables and fruit.

I also produce a lot of vegetable / fruit waste and what I do is use a worm bin. They process the scraps very quick and multiply rapidly, I found it to be a faster way to process organic waste than the traditional compost pile. The wormcastings they produce are one of the best soil amendments.

Yeah we've considered this but we have a vegan kitchen so we must do everything the vegan way. The worms would be fine to use if the bins were on soil so the worms can come and go as they please, but they are not. The bins will be build on a wooden platform.

Edit; thank you though, for thinking with me:)

You need to be adding carbonaceous material in high proportion to veg/fruit matter. Dead leaves, shredded cardboard, straw, etc. The pile will need to be agitated daily. At the scale you're talking, it'll take work to get it all aerated, but it needs to happen. I suggest a pitchfork. The three bin system is a pretty good one. After a month of daily agitation you could move the compost to the other bins, where the remaining decomposition can occur anaerobically with the help of critters (worms, etc). Keep the piles covered from rain to keep from sogging out and to prevent runoff. Good luck and thanks for giving it back!

where the remaining decomposition can occur anaerobically

Does this mean I have to just leave it alone after that month? and how long will it be (aprox) before we can take it out the last bin? Thanks so much for helping me out.

Yes, after a month of regular aeration the compost can do the rest itself. Let it go for about a year before using it in a garden. You want to ensure that seeds have decomposed fully. If you bury the compost instead of top dressing, you could probably use it after the initial month. In that case, bury it under a foot of soil.
